finding: A subtask-order ruling with first == then is ruled and makes the subtask wait on itself forever
why: _order_of checks only that both ids are tracker rows; dependents() omits the subtask itself unless already circular, so keeps_graph is true for first == then.
fix: Refuse (bad-payload or park) when first == then, and test it.
evidence: Probe on a copy: rule(kinds=[subtask-order], first=0001-a, then=0001-a) -> ok ruled=True; next skips 0001-a; start 0001-a -> blocked-by '0001-a waits on 0001-a'. Code: `keeps_graph = first not in dependents(_contracts(plan), then, _order_pairs(state))`

finding: A subtask-order ruling with first == then is ruled and makes the subtask wait on itself for ever
why: AC-072 lets autopilot rule only a call that stays inside the plan; `dependents()` omits the start node, so `keeps_graph` is True for a self pair.
fix: Refuse (bad-payload) or park when `first == then`, and add a test.
evidence: Probe: rule kinds=[subtask-order] first=0001-a then=0001-a -> ruled=True, row set to pending, `start` answers blocked-by, `next` skips it and the run ends with it waiting. Code: keeps_graph = first not in dependents(_contracts(plan), then, _order_pairs(state))

finding: One `no-test` entry turns off the code-before-first-red check for the whole subtask
why: D-76 says `done` refuses a code commit from base to first `red`, but the check runs only when `no_test` is empty, so a mixed subtask (tests plus one prose item) loses it.
fix: Run the early-code check whenever `cycles` is not empty, and add a test with both records.
evidence: Probe: code committed, then `red`, then `no-test`, cycle closed -> verdict() == []. Code: if state["cycles"] and not state["no_test"]: ... Also no check covers code committed between two later cycles (only base..first red is read).

criterion: AC-072 ruling reaches every actor that needs it
finding: A scope ruling is given to the executor only; the review step gets the contract, not the ruling
why: A ruled out-of-Scope file stays outside the contract's `## Scope`, and the `scope` concern asks 'Does it stay inside `## Scope`'; step 6 passes only subtask, plan, change and base, so the review can post or block on the ruled file (reviewer severity for it: unverified).
fix: Tell the review to read `<plan>/DECISIONS.md` rulings for the subtask, or record the ruling where the scope concern reads it.
evidence: walk.py:145 puts rulings only in `brief`; code-review/CONCERNS.md:10 'Does it stay inside `## Scope`'; code-review/SKILL.md:30 'Stay inside the contract's `## Scope`'. Inferred from the text; not run.

finding: The attempt cap (`give_up`) has no test at or around its boundary
why: walk.py:178 returns `give_up=attempts >= ATTEMPT_CAP` and autopilot SKILL.md:27 parks on it, but no test reads `attempts` or `give_up`; changing `>=` to `>` or the cap to 99 passes the whole suite.
fix: Add a test that starts one subtask ATTEMPT_CAP-1 and ATTEMPT_CAP times and asserts `next` gives `give_up` False then True.
evidence: grep for `give_up` and `attempts` in afkv2/tests/skills/test_execute.py, test_autopilot.py and tests/autopilot/test_dry_run.py: 0 hits; walk.py:178 `give_up=attempts >= ATTEMPT_CAP`

finding: Refusal branches of the walk verbs have no test: not-running, already-done, no-such-subtask, base-lost, bad-state, not-feature-branch, and the `status` payload check
why: Input `status` with value `done` (not in STATUS_FLIPS), or `status`/`done` on a pending subtask, should refuse (walk.py:230-233, 421-422), yet no test calls them; the only `status` call is the sunny `reviewing` in the dry run.
fix: Add one negative test per branch: `status` with `done`, `status` and `done` on a pending row, `start` on a done row, `start`/`park` on an unknown id, `done` after the base commit is lost.
evidence: grep for the quoted codes "not-running", "already-done", "no-such-subtask", "base-lost", "bad-state", "not-feature-branch" in the 3 test files: 0 hits

finding: Attempt count survives a park and a human reset, so a retried subtask gets give_up after its first new attempt
why: start does record['attempts'] += 1 on the old record; only a ruling resets it to 0, while next reports attempts 0 for a pending row, so autopilot sees give_up=true right after the 4th start.
fix: Reset the record (or set attempts to 0) when start moves a parked-then-pending row, or count attempts since the last status reset.
evidence: Probe: 3 starts, park, rows set to pending, start -> attempt 4; next -> attempts 4, give_up True. Code: `record['attempts'] += 1` (no cap or reset in start)

finding: A shell builtin first word in a Verification code span (cd) refuses the start as 'not on PATH'
why: _programs takes the first word of every 2+ word span and shutil.which finds no `cd`, although the same cell runs fine through the shell that tdd_log and the executor use; D-71 admits prose spans, not builtins.
fix: Skip shell builtins, or check the first word of each `&&`/`;` segment only for non-builtins.
evidence: Probe: gate_failures on check `cd src && pytest -q` -> gate-cannot-run 'the command `cd` is not on PATH'

finding: v1 scan reads every plan/*.md, including DECISIONS.md and JOURNAL.md that the walk writes, so a ledger line holding '[materialized]' makes the plan a v1 plan for good
why: glob('*.md') minus PLAN.md covers walk.decide/rule/park text, which comes from the executor; the sign then refuses every later check with v1-plan.
fix: Scan only files named in the tracker (the contracts), not the ledger, journal or other run files.
evidence: `for path in sorted(Path(plan).glob("*.md")): if path.name != "PLAN.md" and V1_SEAM_MARK in read_text(path)` (traced by reading; not run)

finding: The v1 seam mark is searched in the whole contract body
why: A v2 contract that quotes `[materialized]` in `## Context excerpts` or prose is refused as a v1 plan with the finish-on-v1 option; D-73 reads no body for a v1 skill name for the same reason.
fix: Search only `## Produces` and `## Consumes` bullets.
evidence: if path.name != "PLAN.md" and V1_SEAM_MARK in read_text(path):  (read from code; not run)

finding: Refusals table omits `no-plan-file` and `no-tracker`, which walk.py verbs can answer
why: `read_text` and `_tracker_table` raise these codes inside every verb; the skill test checks only `Refusal(` codes found in walk.py itself.
fix: Add the 2 codes to the table row of 'correct it, or report it', and scan plan_contract.py in the test.
evidence: plan_contract.py: Refusal("no-plan-file", ...), Refusal("no-tracker", ...); not in the table of SKILL.md

finding: Slice edits files outside the contract ## Scope globs (wiring IOU file, plan-s3 DECISIONS/JOURNAL/PLAN)
why: Scope lists only afkv2/skills/{autopilot,execute}/**, 2 test files and afkv2/tests/autopilot/**; the diff also touches .claude/wiring-ious.md and 3 plan-s3 ledger files.
fix: Accept as protocol-required ledger writes (IOU rule, DECISIONS.md protocol), or add them to ## Scope in the contract.
evidence: ## Scope: afkv2/skills/autopilot/** ... afkv2/tests/autopilot/**  # fakes + fixtures for this slice only; git diff --stat shows .claude/wiring-ious.md, docs/afk/afkv2/plan-s3/{DECISIONS,JOURNAL,PLAN}.md

criterion: blast radius: callers of a contract the diff changed
finding: IOU for forge verb auth-status still says the live round trip is its only caller; start_gate.py now calls it
why: start_gate.forge_answer runs `ports/forge/cli.py auth-status` (start_gate.py:192-198), so the 'only caller' claim and the keep-or-remove question at the feature gate are stale.
fix: Edit the line: auth-status has a code caller in start_gate.py (forge_failures); keep thread-list in the IOU alone.
evidence: - [ ] `afkv2/ports/forge/cli.py` verbs `thread-list`, `auth-status` -> anchor: contract "afkv2/tests/ports/live/forge_round_trip.py" is the only caller

finding: Possible mock echo: the `no-approval` count of 2 pins the fake's own re-implementation of the approval check
why: fake_check_plan.py:31-36 invents a `no-approval` failure, so `codes.count("no-approval") == 2` passes on the fake's behaviour; the real check_plan (S2, unbuilt, D-72 says the form is unverified) may use another code or none, and the assertion then fails or hides a double report.
fix: Assert `"no-approval" in codes` plus the other failures, and keep the count out until the real check_plan answers.
evidence: `assert codes.count("no-approval") == 2  # the check's own failure and the gate's`; fake_check_plan.py: `failure = {"code": "no-approval", ...}`

finding: The `run` fixture stubs `ci_state` to `watching` for every test, so the real CI-state path runs only for `none`
why: Every `done` success test in this file passes with an invented state; the real `lost` and `no-verdict` states of ci_watch.py:166 and :207 are never fed to `done`, and the dry run stubs `finished` too (test_dry_run.py:69).
fix: Add a test that feeds `lost` and `no-verdict` to `done` and pins the intended result (accept or refuse).
evidence: `monkeypatch.setattr(walk, "ci_state", lambda change: "watching")`; walk.py:404 `elif ci_state(change) in (None, "none")`

finding: A test is coupled to the text of this slice's own contract and skips itself when the plan folder is gone
why: It asserts exact blocker ids, produces tuples and tier order of 0015-autopilot-execute.md, so any contract edit breaks it, and after `/afk:gc` deletes the folder the parser check silently becomes a skip.
fix: Parse a contract built by `contract_text` instead, or keep a committed fixture copy of the frozen sections.
evidence: `path = next(REPOSITORY.glob("docs/*/afkv2/plan-s3/0015-autopilot-execute.md"), None)`; `pytest.skip("the plan folder of this build has left the tree")`

finding: Skill-text tests loop and branch inside the test body, and check prose by bare substring
why: The `if code != "bad-payload"` inside a `for` hides which code failed, and substrings such as `"Ship"` (test_autopilot.py:408) match anywhere in the file, so a deleted section still passes.
fix: Parameterize over the verbs and codes, and match a heading or a backticked form.
evidence: `for code in re.findall(r'Refusal("([a-z-]+)"', source): if code != "bad-payload": assert f"`{code}`" in text`

finding: The `run` fixture docstring says a plan of 3 but the fixture builds 4 subtasks
why: A reader who trusts the docstring misreads tests that rely on `0004-d` as the independent subtask.
fix: Change the docstring to 4 subtasks and name 0004-d.
evidence: `"""A plan of 3: 0001-a, then 0002-b ... 0004-d waits on nothing."""` followed by 4 entries

finding: Only the `e2e` and `api` spellings of LIVE_TIERS are tested; `browser`, `e2e/browser` and `ui-e2e` and the case folding are not
why: start_gate.py:30,179 lists 5 live tiers and lowercases the tier; deleting 3 of them or the `.lower()` leaves the suite green.
fix: Parameterize test_a_live_tier_with_no_app_refuses_before_any_work over every LIVE_TIERS member plus `E2E`.
evidence: `LIVE_TIERS = {"api", "e2e", "browser", "e2e/browser", "ui-e2e"}`; tests use only `| e2e |` and `| api |`

finding: The rename branch of `_uncommitted` (`skip = entry[0] in "RC"`) has no test
why: A staged rename of a test file (`R  tests/b` then `tests/a`) is the only input that reaches that branch; a wrong skip would call a test rename a code change and refuse `red` with `code-before-red`.
fix: Add a `red` test after `git mv tests/test_a.py tests/test_b.py` that expects success.
evidence: tdd_log.py:81-84 `skip = entry[0] in "RC"`; test_red_refuses_when_code_changed_first_and_allows_a_new_test_file covers only a new file

finding: A bare `- ` line in `## Blocked by` raises IndexError, and the check answers 'internal' instead of listing failures
why: bullets() yields '' for '- ' and blocked_by does bullet.split()[0] on it; contracts_of and walk callers do not catch it.
fix: Skip empty bullets in bullets() or blocked_by.
evidence:
Probe: Contract('x', {'Blocked by': '- 0001-a
- 
- 0002-b'}).blocked_by -> IndexError: list index out of range

finding: A repeated red on an open cycle moves its head forward; verdict then counts later commits as before the first red
why: red overwrites cycle['red'] with the current HEAD, and verdict uses cycles[0]['red']['head'] as the bound, so code committed after the first red and before the re-run is flagged code-before-red.
fix: Keep the first head of an open cycle (setdefault), and use the earliest head across cycles.
evidence: `cycle.update(command=command, red={"head": ...})` and `first_red = state["cycles"][0]["red"]["head"]` (traced by reading; not run)

finding: done on an in-flight row with no run.json record raises KeyError, answered as 'internal'
why: state['subtasks'][subtask] is indexed directly; a row set to developing by hand (or a lost run.json) has no record.
fix: Refuse with a named code (e.g. no-start-record) when the record is absent.
evidence: `_finish_failures(plan, subtask, state["subtasks"][subtask], state["change"])` (traced by reading; not run)
